answer: Every new identity takes a numbered turn at a tidal inlet registrar that admits one applicant per tide, starving burst sign-ups. Privileges lapse unless the agent keeps an inhabited island of independently billed counterparties who countersign live work, and payouts unlock only when an ocean-crossing shipment is receipted by a buyer outside that island. Copies sharing a dispatcher reuse the same inlet ticket and the same customer island, and the registrar freezes the set. N identities therefore cost N inlet turns, N islands of real buyers, and N actual ocean shipments.
